question: Clinics selling unproven stem cell interventions try to look scientifically legitimate. Name one way they do this.
answers: They point to animal studies as proof it works
They seek token approval from dubious for-profit ethics boards
They list the treatments as pay-to-participate trials on ClinicalTrials.gov

receipt.quote: Many of these clinics use fake scientific articles or point to animal studies to demonstrate treatment efficacy (Richey and Frow, 2019), seek dubious for-profit ethics boards for token approval (Knoepfler, 2019c), and list unproven SCIs as pay-to-participate trials on ClinicalTrials.gov since the registry is not monitored (Turner, 2017).

question: How does media hype about stem cell research help the unproven stem cell clinic industry grow?
answers: It makes the public think stem cell therapies are or will soon be available, and some clinics exploit that belief to market unproven interventions instead of investing in clinical research

receipt.quote: The media hype suggesting that stem cell research will lead to novel cures creates a public perception that stem cell therapies are or will soon be available (Caulfield et al., 2016; Kamenova and Caulfield, 2015). Rather than undertaking the substantive investment necessary to ensure cell therapies are safe and effective through clinical research, some clinics have taken advantage of this public perception to market unproven SCIs.
